items.answer: Vuforia is a tracking library that has an augmented reality (AR) plugin that works with Unity three-dimensional (3D) and can be used to create AR applications, particularly mobile AR applications for iOS and Android platforms.
A collider in Unity configured as a trigger using the isTrigger property does not behave as a solid object and simply allows other colliders to pass through.
The Unity physics engine includes rigid bodies, colliders, joints, physics articulation, and character controllers as components essential to give a realistic feeling.
Augmented reality on the reality-virtuality continuum is the intermediate state in which the real environment is augmented with virtual content.

Marker-based augmented reality (AR) applications use markers placed in the environment to trigger an augmented experience, and when a device detects a marker, the desired digital content appears at that marker's position in the real-world view.

Virtual reality (VR) is, according to the Miriam Webster dictionary, an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli, in which sights and sounds play a primary role and are provided by a computer, possibly along with other sensory stimuli, and in which a person's actions partially determine what happens in the environment.

questions.question: Why would a developer write scripts in Unity instead of relying only on built-in support?
options: To change the built-in support for a more customized experience
To make the Unity scripting environment install automatically
To replace the Unity package with a different development environment
To turn a game object into a separate visual asset
questions.explanation: Built-in support gives only the experience that the system provides, so scripts or small pieces of code are used to change it to match the programmer's expectations and needs.

questions.question: How is Unity's C# scripting environment initially available in a project?
options: It is set up automatically when the Unity package is installed
The developer must manually install a compatible IDE first
It is created by choosing Assets, then Create, then C# Script
It becomes available only after a script asset is opened
questions.explanation: Unity's scripting environment is set up automatically with the Unity package, and supported IDEs can then be used to develop and compile scripts.

questions.question: What happens to a C# script that is attached to a game object in Unity?
options: It is activated only while the developer edits the scene
It remains a standalone asset until the project is exported
It replaces the game object with a prefab before execution
It is treated as a component and starts working whenever the game is executed
questions.explanation: A C# script is essentially a new type of component that can be attached to a game object, and once attached it starts working whenever the game is executed.

questions.question: What can a developer do with a C# script once it is running in a Unity game?
options: It can block user input from reaching the game object
It can trigger events, modify properties over time, and respond to user input
It can edit the installed Unity package while the game runs
It can modify only the project panel after the game ends
questions.explanation: Once the game is executed, an attached C# script allows the developer to trigger game events, modify component properties over time, and respond to user input as desired.

questions.question: Unlike most other assets, how are C# scripts usually created in Unity?
options: By importing an existing script asset from another project
By manually saving a code file in the Unity installation folder
By choosing GameObject, then Create, then C# Script
Directly within Unity by choosing Assets, then Create, then C# Script
questions.explanation: C# scripts are usually created directly in Unity using the IDE interface, via Assets > Create > C# Script, and are placed in the project folder selected when the project starts.

data.text: To obtain a more customized experience, programmers must write scripts to change the built-in support. Unity supports the object-oriented language C# and usually includes an integrated development environment. These scripts can be attached as components to game objects to control behavior and respond to user input. Scripts are usually created directly within the Unity environment.
points: Custom scripts are needed to provide a more customized experience than the built-in support provides.
Unity supports C#, an object-oriented programming language, and usually includes an integrated development environment.
C# scripts function as components that can be attached to game objects to control behavior and respond to user input.
Scripts are usually created directly within Unity using the Assets menu.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the main class in a typical Unity C# script file?
options: A public class inheriting MonoBehaviour, named the same as the file
A private class inheriting MonoBehaviour, named differently from the file
A public class inheriting MonoBehaviour, named the same as the folder
A public class not inheriting MonoBehaviour, named the same as the file
questions.explanation: A Unity C# script file defines a public class, typically inherited from MonoBehaviour, and the class name is the same as the file name.

questions.question: In a Unity script, what is the role of the Update function?
options: It is called once as the starting point when the script is called
It destroys a game object after a specified delay
It prints a message to the console output after the game runs
It is called in each frame while the script executes
questions.explanation: The Update function is called in each frame and is invoked whenever the script executes and some change happens.

questions.question: In a Unity script, what does the Vector3 data type represent?
options: The position of a 3D point using three coordinates
The rotation of a 3D object using three coordinates
The position of a 2D point using two coordinates
The scale of a 3D object using one coordinate
questions.explanation: Vector3 represents the position of a three-dimensional point by storing three coordinates as three elements of a vector.

questions.question: In Unity, how can a developer check variable values in a script?
options: In the project panel after creating a C# script
In the code file after double-clicking the script asset
In the Inspector interface on the Unity Hub editor
In the console output after the script has been executed
questions.explanation: A developer can check variable values in the Inspector interface on the Unity Hub editor.

questions.question: What does the Debug.Log function do in a Unity script?
options: It destroys a game object after a specified delay
It checks variable values in the Inspector interface
It prints a message to the console output
It creates a new C# script in the selected folder
questions.explanation: Debug.Log prints a message to the console output, which can be seen after running the game or application or after the script has been executed.

data.text: A Unity C# script begins with namespaces and a public class that typically inherits from MonoBehaviour, using Start and Update functions to run code at the beginning and every frame. Vector3 is used to represent coordinates for a 3D point, while the Inspector and Debug.Log function allow for checking variables and printing messages to the console.
points: A Unity C# script begins with namespaces, using statements, and a public class that typically inherits from MonoBehaviour.
Scripts use a Start function to run at the beginning and an Update function to run every frame.
Vector3 is a data type used to represent the coordinates of a 3D point.
Developers can view code by double-clicking a script and check variables in the Inspector interface.
The Debug.Log function prints messages to the console output.

questions.question: What does the Unity Destroy function do to a game object?
options: It destroys the object immediately when the script starts.
It hides the object permanently without removing it from the scene.
It makes the object visible only while the delay is active.
It destroys the object after a specified delay, typically in seconds.
questions.explanation: The Destroy function, which comes under MonoBehaviour, destroys a game object from the scene after a specified delay, typically in seconds.

questions.question: In a Unity script, what is the role difference between prebuilt functions and user-defined functions?
options: Prebuilt functions are optional improvements, while user-defined functions are required for the script to work.
Prebuilt functions are defined by the user, while user-defined functions are supplied automatically by Unity.
Prebuilt functions are used only for initialization, while user-defined functions are used only for update events.
Prebuilt functions are critical for making the script work, while user-defined functions are defined by the user and are typically part of a good script.
questions.explanation: Unity scripts use prebuilt functions that are critical for making a script work, and user-defined functions, which are defined by the user and are typically part of a good script.

questions.question: What happens when a Unity gameplay event occurs for an event function?
options: The event function's body executes and then retains control instead of returning it to Unity.
Unity executes the event function before the gameplay event occurs, so it can prepare in advance.
Unity passes control to the event function, executes its body, then returns control to Unity.
The developer manually calls the event function after detecting the gameplay event.
questions.explanation: An event function is activated by Unity in response to a gameplay event: Unity passes control to the function, its body executes, and then control is passed back to Unity.

questions.question: When are OnTriggerEnter, OnTriggerStay, and OnTriggerExit functions called in Unity?
options: When the script runs its regular update functions each frame.
When the GUI receives a mouse-over or mouse-down event.
When a collider is configured as a trigger.
When a physics collision registers contact being made or broken.
questions.explanation: OnTriggerEnter, OnTriggerStay, and OnTriggerExit are other physics-related event functions that are called when a collider is configured as a trigger.

questions.question: How can Unity event functions be used to impose realistic behavior?
options: Physics-event functions can impose visual behavior, while GUI event functions can impose user-input behavior.
Physics-event functions can impose interactive behavior, while GUI event functions can impose physical behavior.
Physics-event functions can impose rendering behavior, while GUI event functions can impose physical behavior.
Physics-event functions can impose physical behavior, while GUI event functions can impose interactive behavior.
questions.explanation: Unity's event functions can impose realistic behavior, such as physical behavior in physics-event functions and interactive behavior in GUI event functions.

data.text: Unity scripts use prebuilt and user-defined functions, including the Destroy function which destroys a game object from the scene after a specified delay. Event functions are activated by Unity in response to gameplay events such as regular updates, initialization, graphical user interface, and physics events. These functions are used to impose realistic and interactive behaviors.
points: The Destroy function destroys a game object from the scene after a specified delay.
Unity scripts use both prebuilt functions and user-defined functions.
Event functions are activated by Unity in response to gameplay events, where Unity passes control to the function and then back to Unity.
Common gameplay events include regular updates, initialization, graphical user interface, and physics events.
Event functions can be used to impose realistic and interactive behaviors.

questions.question: What must a script contain in order to instantiate a prefab at runtime?
options: A reference to a coroutine
A reference to a transform component
A reference to a scene
A reference to that prefab
questions.explanation: Runtime instantiation of a prefab requires the script being written to have a reference to that prefab.

questions.question: In the editor, how is a prefab attached to a script for runtime instantiation?
options: After adding the script to a game object, drag the prefab from the project window into the script component's My Prefab field
After adding the script to a game object, drag the prefab from the project window into the hierarchy window
After adding the script to a game object, drag the script from the project window into the prefab's My Prefab field
After adding the script to a game object, drag the prefab from the project window into the scene view
questions.explanation: The prefab is attached for runtime instantiation by dragging it from the project window into the script component's My Prefab field.

questions.question: How is a do-while loop different from a for loop or while loop?
options: Its condition is checked after the body, so the body runs at least once
Its condition is checked before the body, so the body may not run
It is used to work directly with a collection of homogeneous data types
It is entry-controlled because its condition is checked after the body
questions.explanation: For and while loops are entry-controlled because their condition is checked before the body executes, while a do-while loop is exit-controlled because its body executes at least once and its condition is checked after the body.

questions.question: What is a foreach loop used for in the scripting environment?
options: Working directly with an array or collection of homogeneous data types
Pausing execution and continuing on the following frame
Working directly with a single transform component's position, rotation, and scale
Checking a loop condition before any loop body executes
questions.explanation: A foreach loop can be used for arrays or collections of homogeneous data types, allowing the programmer to work with the collection directly instead of dealing with individual data types.

data.text: To instantiate a prefab at runtime, a script needs a reference that is attached in the editor by dragging the prefab into a script component's field. Script behavior can be controlled using standard if-else statements and various loop types, including entry-controlled for and while loops, exit-controlled do-while loops, and foreach loops for collections of homogeneous data types.
points: A script needs a reference to a prefab to instantiate it at runtime.
Prefabs are attached in the editor by dragging them into a script component's field.
The scripting environment supports standard if-else statements.
For and while loops are entry-controlled, while do-while loops are exit-controlled.
Foreach loops can be used for arrays or collections of homogeneous data types.

questions.question: Which three values are stored in a game object's Transform property?
options: Position, rotation, and scale
Calibration and registration values
Initial delay and repeat interval
Viewer pose and anchor position
questions.explanation: The Transform property stores a game object's position, rotation, and scale.

questions.question: How does a Unity coroutine spread a task over several frames?
options: It starts a separate thread for each task.
It registers virtual content by determining the viewer's pose.
It calls a function after a delay and then at fixed intervals.
It pauses execution, returns control to Unity, and resumes on a later frame.
questions.explanation: A coroutine spreads work across frames by pausing, returning control to Unity, and continuing where it left off.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes coroutines from threads?
options: A coroutine spawns one thread for each paused operation.
Coroutines execute on the main thread and do not spawn individual threads.
A coroutine is designed to behave like a thread for background work.
A coroutine pauses the main thread so other threads can run.
questions.explanation: Coroutines are not threads; synchronous operations inside them still run on the main thread.

questions.question: What makes a gradual opacity fade visible?
options: Changing the object's Transform values instead of its opacity.
Reducing the alpha or opacity value over a sequence of frames.
Calling the fade function once with the final opacity value.
Invoking the fade method on a separate thread.
questions.explanation: A fade is perceivable only when its alpha or opacity changes frame by frame so Unity renders intermediate values.

questions.question: What do the two times passed to InvokeRepeating specify?
options: The viewer's pose and anchor position.
The initial delay before the first call and the interval between repeated calls.
The first frame and last frame of the animation.
The object's local scale and rotation values.
questions.explanation: InvokeRepeating takes a function name and two times: the initial start time and the repeat interval.

data.text: The transform property allows for the programmatic modification of an object's position, rotation, and scale. Coroutines spread tasks across several frames by pausing and resuming, but they are not threads and execute on the main thread. Because changes must be spread over multiple frames to be perceivable, opacity fades must be defined as coroutines. Additionally, InvokeRepeating can be used to execute a method after a delay and at regular intervals.
points: The transform property stores an object's position, rotation, and scale and can be modified programmatically.
Coroutines spread tasks across several frames by pausing and resuming execution.
Coroutines are not threads and run on the main thread.
Opacity fades must be defined as coroutines to spread changes over multiple frames.
InvokeRepeating executes a method after a delay and at regular intervals.

questions.question: In Unity, how is user input from devices supported?
options: Imported SDK input support replaces Unity's inbuilt handling of the mouse, keyboard, and buttons.
A coroutine extends Unity's inbuilt input handling for other device-specific inputs.
Unity provides inbuilt handling for every input device, so imported SDK input support is unnecessary.
Unity provides inbuilt handling for inputs such as the mouse, keyboard, and buttons, while imported SDK input support may extend it for other device-specific inputs.
questions.explanation: Unity has inbuilt handling for common inputs, and imported SDK input support can extend that inbuilt support for other device-specific inputs.

questions.question: In the Unity development environment, what is the last stage after a script is written and the system is built?
options: Selecting the platform to which the system is deployed.
Managing which scenes are included in the build.
Publishing or deploying the system.
Beginning the build process with a build button.
questions.explanation: The last stage is to publish or deploy the system, with the Build Settings window containing the settings and options for publishing the build.

questions.question: In Unity's Build Settings window, which element begins the build process?
options: The Build or Build and Run button.
The platform section.
The My Prefab field.
The Scenes in Build panel.
questions.explanation: The Build or Build and Run button begins the build process, while the Scenes in Build panel manages included scenes and the platform section selects the deployment platform.

data.text: Unity supports inputs like the mouse and keyboard, but other device-specific inputs may need an SDK. The Build Settings window is used to publish or deploy the system after the script is written and the system is built. This window manages which scenes are included, selects the target platform, and begins the build process.
points: Unity supports inputs like the mouse and keyboard, while other devices may need an SDK.
The Build Settings window is used to publish or deploy the system.
This window manages the included scenes, the target platform, and the build process.

questions.question: When is importing a platform-specific SDK or package used for deployment on an HMD or smart glasses?
options: When the target platform provides functions that are already included in Unity's built-in support
When the application is marker-based augmented reality rather than markerless augmented reality
When the target platform provides functions that are not included in Unity's built-in support
When the deployment target is a head-mounted display rather than smart glasses
questions.explanation: A developer imports SDKs or packages when the specified hardware platform offers platform-specific functions that Unity's built-in support does not include.

questions.question: How is the SDK layer positioned in Unity's layered architecture?
options: It is below the Unity layer and above the application layer
It is inside the application layer and below the Unity layer
It is above the application layer and below the Unity layer
It is on top of the Unity layer and below the application layer
questions.explanation: The application is the top layer, while the SDK layer sits on top of the Unity layer and is treated as part of the installed Unity package.

questions.question: What is Vuforia mainly intended to help developers with?
options: Extending Unity's inbuilt mouse, keyboard, and button input handling
Managing scenes and platform selection in Unity's Build Settings window
Virtual-reality head tracking and controller input for immersive virtual environments
Augmented-reality object recognition and computer-vision tasks such as detection, recognition, and tracking
questions.explanation: Vuforia is an AR SDK primarily meant to help developers deal with object recognition or computer vision issues, including object detection, recognition, and tracking.

questions.question: Why may efficient object recognition require an external package in Unity?
options: Because Unity's built-in support for object detection, recognition, and tracking is not extensive or very good
Because the SDK layer must be placed below the Unity layer for recognition to work
Because Unity's built-in support for object recognition is completely absent
Because object recognition requires a marker-based augmented reality application rather than a markerless one
questions.explanation: Unity's built-in support for object recognition or computer vision operations is not extensive and not very good, so efficient performance requires external packages.

questions.question: Which sequence describes the basic steps for integrating an SDK into Unity?
options: Import the SDK package, install Unity Hub, compile, build, and deploy, then use the functions
Install Unity Hub, compile, build, and deploy, import the SDK package, then use the functions
Install Unity Hub, import the SDK package, use Unity and SDK functions, compile, build, and deploy
Use Unity and SDK functions, install Unity Hub, import the SDK package, compile, build, and deploy
questions.explanation: The basic integration steps are to install Unity Hub, import the SDK package, use both Unity and SDK functions, and then compile, build, and deploy.

data.text: Developers import SDKs to access platform-specific functions that Unity does not provide natively. In the software architecture, the SDK layer sits between the application and the Unity layer. Because Unity's built-in support for computer vision is not extensive, external packages like Vuforia are required for efficient performance. The integration process involves installing Unity Hub, importing the package, using the functions, and then compiling, building, and deploying the system.
points: Developers import SDKs to access platform-specific functions not included in Unity's built-in support.
The SDK layer is positioned between the application layer and the Unity layer in the software architecture.
External packages like Vuforia are required for efficient computer vision because Unity's built-in support is not extensive.
The basic steps for SDK integration involve installing Unity Hub, importing the package, using the functions, and then compiling, building, and deploying.

questions.question: What type of toolkit is Vuforia when used with Unity for augmented reality?
options: An Android-only AR SDK that does not support iOS
A 3D modeling app that creates Unity assets
A cross-platform VR SDK for fully virtual environments
A licensed, cross-platform AR SDK for computer-vision tracking
questions.explanation: Vuforia is an AR SDK that supports advanced computer vision for recognizing images and objects, and it is cross-platform and requires a license.

questions.question: Why must a Vuforia database be created and imported into the Unity project before image targets can be recognized?
options: It changes the project's graphics API and ARM settings
It contains the images or markers that the Vuforia engine is to recognize
It stores the Unity project's Vuforia license key
It keeps the downloaded 3D model files for the sample
questions.explanation: The database is created to add the tracked images or markers, and the database package is imported because it is required for recognition.

questions.question: When does an image target behavior script perform its operations in a Vuforia sample?
options: During the selection of the Unity project template
After the Vuforia engine has recognized the marker
While the 3D model is being scaled in the Inspector
Before the target image is added to the Vuforia database
questions.explanation: The script is attached to the image target and performs its operations after the Vuforia engine recognizes the marker.

questions.question: In the Unity sample scene, how is a 3D model associated with a recognized image target?
options: The target image and 3D model are assigned to the image target component, and the model is scaled
The target image and 3D model are placed in folders, but no component assignment is needed
The target image is assigned to the Vuforia AR camera, and the model is attached to the script
The 3D model is assigned to the main camera, and the image target is scaled
questions.explanation: The sample scene assigns the target image asset and the 3D model to the image target component, then scales the model in the Inspector.

questions.question: For the Android sample, what must be done before choosing Build and Run so the APK is deployed directly to the device?
options: Create the Vuforia database, connect the device by USB, and enable USB debugging
Select the iOS platform, connect the device by USB, and enable USB debugging
Select the Android platform, connect the device by USB, and enable USB debugging
Import the 3D model, connect the device by USB, and enable USB debugging
questions.explanation: For Android, the build process requires switching to the Android platform and connecting the device through a USB cable with USB debugging enabled; then Build and Run deploys the APK directly.

data.text: Vuforia is a cross-platform SDK that provides computer vision functionality for recognizing images and objects in AR. Developers must install the SDK, configure a license and database, and set up the AR camera and 3D models in Unity. Finally, specific player settings and build processes are used to deploy the application, which recognizes markers to display 3D models.
points: Vuforia is a cross-platform SDK that provides computer vision functionality for recognizing images and objects in AR.
Setup involves creating a Unity project, adding the SDK, and importing a license and database.
Building the scene requires configuring the AR camera, assigning 3D models to targets, and attaching behavior scripts.
Specific player settings and build processes are needed to deploy the application to an Android device.
The application recognizes markers to display matching 3D models.

questions.question: In building a virtual or augmented reality system, what determines the amount of programming involved?
options: The required functionality of the system
The selected headset
The imported 3D model
The targeted application domain
questions.explanation: The amount of programming depends on the required functionality: basic systems can be built with menu-based IDE support, while customized experiences require scripting.

questions.question: When can a basic virtual or augmented reality system be built without scripting?
options: When the required features exceed Unity support
When a device-specific SDK is imported
When a customized experience is required
When its basic functionalities are built using menu-based IDE support
questions.explanation: A basic system with basic functionalities can be built without scripting using menu-based IDE support; a customized experience requires scripting.

questions.question: Why are software development kits imported when developing virtual or augmented reality systems?
options: To remove the Unity main camera
To configure the Android OpenGL API
To provide device-specific support when Unity's built-in support is insufficient
To upload the Vuforia image database
questions.explanation: SDKs provide device-specific support and are imported when the required functionalities exceed the support provided by the Unity development environment.

questions.question: What do the Programmer's Manual and Developer's Manual provide for virtual and augmented reality development?
options: Further details on building, deploying, and writing code
Device-specific input data
A Vuforia image-recognition license
A list of XR application domains
questions.explanation: The Programmer's Manual and Developer's Manual provide further details on building and deploying virtual and augmented reality systems and writing code.

data.text: Building and deploying XR systems are programming tasks where the amount of programming depends on the required functionality, ranging from menu-based IDE support to scripting. questions.question: Why can a basic virtual or augmented reality system be built in Unity without scripting, while a customized experience requires scripting?
questions.reference_answer: Unity's built-in support gives a good-quality experience, but only what the system provides, so a programmer must write scripts to change it. Building and deploying virtual and augmented reality systems are primarily programming tasks, with the amount depending on required functionality. A basic system with basic functionalities can be built without scripting using menu-based integrated development environment support, whereas a customized experience requires scripting and therefore more programming.

questions.question: How does a C# script attached to a Unity game object let a developer create realistic interactive behavior during game execution?
questions.reference_answer: A C# script can be attached as a component to a game object, and creating the script is essentially creating a new type of component that behaves as the developer wants. Once attached, it starts working when the game is executed, allowing the developer to trigger game events, modify component properties over time, and respond to user input. Unity event functions can then impose realistic behavior, such as interactive behavior in graphical user interface event functions.

questions.question: Why must a gradual opacity fade of a Unity object be implemented as a coroutine rather than a fade function that is called only once?
questions.reference_answer: A coroutine is a method that spreads tasks across several frames by pausing execution, returning control to Unity, and continuing where it left off on the following frame. A gradual opacity fade is visible only when its opacity value is reduced over a sequence of frames so Unity can render the intermediate values. A fade function called only once is not perceivable, so the fade must be defined as a coroutine and started so the change is spread frame by frame.

questions.question: How does Vuforia enable marker-based augmented reality in Unity when Unity's built-in support for object recognition is limited?
questions.reference_answer: Unity's built-in support for object recognition or computer vision operations is not extensive and not very good, so seamless and efficient performance requires external packages. Vuforia is an augmented reality software development kit that supports advanced computer vision for recognizing images and objects and interacting with spaces in the real world. In marker-based augmented reality, a marker triggers the experience, and when the Vuforia engine recognizes the matching image, it displays a three-dimensional model in place of the marker.
